newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell chief admits mistakes in public relations.
newsitem.headline: Shell chief admits mistakes in public relations.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Chairman Cor Herkstroter said on Friday the company had mishandled recent controversies by not providing the public or pressure groups with adequate information.

"We were, perhaps, excessively focused on internal matters, and we failed to fully understand the need to provide information to the general public. So, we tended to become inward looking, isolated and consequently some have seen us as a 'state within a state'," Herkstroter told an audience at the Amsterdam Department for the Association of International Affairs.
Henkstroter said the company had been slow to appreciate the growing influence of pressure groups.
"We failed to engage in serious dialogue with these new groups," he said
He also said the company had learnt that it cannot tackle public relations matters in the same way as technical problems. There was, he said, rarely a single correct answer.
However, he said that in a world of increasing political, social and economic liberalisation, conflicting opinions abounded.
"Expectations are very rarely consistent. We are sometimes expected to behave in one way in one part of the world and rather differently in another part," he said.
He also said, with reference to Nigeria, that while that Shell has ethical standards, it does not have the power or the responsibility to influence political events.
"We are a business. We are not a social, political or moral authority," he said.
Shell has been embroiled in controversy over its planned deep sea disposal of the Brent Spar platform in the North Sea and its operations in Nigeria.
